doc.title: John Abercrombie interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001

title: How his playing has changed with the trio
summary: Hearing old recordings, he feels he has more control and maturity now, if a little less wild.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: I’m glad you listened to that today because you anticipated one of my questions.
That was if you listen to a tape of tonight’s performance, whatever happens, and then you listen to what you guys were doing seven or eight years ago, how does it change?

I think what changes for me is just that, I mean usually we’re off all doing different things and then we come back together and I find that either with this band or with other bands, just hopefully you get better. I think I find I’m able to — my phrasing is a little

different, I have a little more control over what I do than I did when that album was recorded, and if I listen to that album and go back and listen to something earlier I realize oh, boy I had much more control when we recorded the live album. So I think what happens is you just get the ability to, at least I do, to shape things as they’re happening a little more. You get a little more mature. Maybe you’re not quite as wild and crazy you know. But there’s still that element in there too.
